title: Advanced Excel and Power Query Laboratory
description: Eight progressive healthcare analytics spreadsheet challenges with worked solutions, synthetic source data and a timed client simulation.

challenges.title: Logical and conditional formulas
challenges.scenario: The quality lead needs a transparent list of longer-stay encounters and department-level counts.
tasks: Add a Long_Stay_Flag column to the encounter table using IF; use >7 days as a training threshold only.
Count encounters in each department using COUNTIF or COUNTIFS.
Use IFERROR to make lookup or division failures explicit rather than hiding them.
challenges.hint: Use structured references inside Excel Tables. Keep the threshold visible and label it as an operational exercise, not a clinical rule.
challenges.solution: Long-stay flag: =IF([@length_of_stay_days]>7,"Review","Within threshold"). Department count: =COUNTIF(tblEncounters[department],A2). Safe ratio: =IFERROR(numerator/denominator,0), but explain why zero is an appropriate fallback; otherwise return NA() or a clear text state.
challenges.expected: 80 encounter rows; mean LOS 3.875 days. Exact long-stay count can be independently checked with COUNTIF against the supplied LOS column.
acceptance: Formula is filled down to all 80 encounters.
No hard-coded department totals.
Threshold and denominator are documented.
Errors are not silently converted into misleading values.

challenges.title: Conditional aggregation with SUMIFS and AVERAGEIFS
challenges.scenario: An operations analyst needs order quantities by status and mean length of stay by department.
tasks: Calculate total ordered quantity for Active orders with SUMIFS.
Calculate mean LOS for each department using AVERAGEIFS.
Add a second criterion, such as payer type, to a department summary.
challenges.hint: Raw status contains inconsistent casing/whitespace. Compare pre-clean and post-clean results, and do not silently exclude records.
challenges.solution: After normalising status, use =SUMIFS(tblCleanOrders[quantity],tblCleanOrders[order_status],"Active"). Mean LOS: =AVERAGEIFS(tblEncounters[length_of_stay_days],tblEncounters[department],A2). Multiple criteria can be appended as criteria_range, criteria pairs.
challenges.expected: Use Reference_Checks for global controls. Your department/status totals depend on cleaning rules; document them and reconcile row counts before comparing.
acceptance: Uses SUMIFS/AVERAGEIFS rather than manual filtering.
Documents missing-value treatment and criteria.
Totals reconcile to the cleaned dataset.
No confusion between order quantity and administered dose.

challenges.title: XLOOKUP and INDEX/MATCH
challenges.scenario: The pharmacy analytics team needs a consistent therapeutic-class mapping from a synthetic reference table.
tasks: Clean drug_name text before matching.
Return standard_therapeutic_class and reference_unit_cost_inr using XLOOKUP.
Recreate the class lookup using INDEX/MATCH for compatibility.
challenges.hint: TRIM removes leading/trailing spaces; CLEAN removes nonprinting characters. Standardise case consistently on both sides or use a case-insensitive exact match (Excel's standard text match is case-insensitive).
challenges.solution: Create Clean_Drug_Name = TRIM(CLEAN([@drug_name])). Then use =XLOOKUP([@Clean_Drug_Name],tblFormulary[drug_name],tblFormulary[standard_therapeutic_class],"Not found",0). INDEX/MATCH equivalent: =IFERROR(INDEX(tblFormulary[standard_therapeutic_class],MATCH([@Clean_Drug_Name],tblFormulary[drug_name],0)),"Not found").
challenges.expected: All formulary-listed drugs should map after text cleaning. Unmatched values remain visibly Not found for investigation.
acceptance: Exact-match lookup used.
Text cleaned before lookup.
Unmatched values are retained and reviewed.
Lookup output does not overwrite source data.

challenges.title: PivotTables and PivotCharts
challenges.scenario: A hospital manager wants a compact view of encounter distribution and medication-order mix.
tasks: Build an encounter count PivotTable with department as rows and payer_type as columns.
Build an order count PivotTable with therapeutic_class as rows and order_status as columns.
Add a PivotChart and at least one filter/slicer if supported.
challenges.starter:
Pivot 1: Rows = department; Columns = payer_type; Values = Count of encounter_id.
Pivot 2: Rows = therapeutic_class; Columns = order_status; Values = Count of order_id.
challenges.hint: Use Count, not Sum, for identifier fields. Refresh PivotTables after Power Query refresh. A PivotTable can only be as trustworthy as its source grain and cleaning steps.
challenges.solution: Excel: select a cell in the table > Insert > PivotTable > New Worksheet. Drag the specified fields to Rows, Columns and Values. Set Values to Count. Insert PivotChart from the PivotTable. Add slicers for department or status if available. Linux: LibreOffice Data > Pivot Table > Insert/Edit; menus and slicer support differ.
challenges.expected: Encounter PivotTable grand total should be 80. Raw order PivotTable total should be 151 before deduplication; cleaned total depends on the explicitly documented duplicate rule.
acceptance: Correct fields and Count aggregation.
Grand totals tie to source or cleaned row counts.
Chart title, units and filters are clear.
Refresh behaviour is understood.

challenges.title: Power Query cleaning and transformation
challenges.scenario: A monthly extract has inconsistent text, missing fields, a duplicate-like record and an orphan encounter reference.
tasks: Import the three CSVs with Data > Get Data > From Text/CSV.
Set explicit data types; trim/clean text; standardise order_status casing.
Identify and remove exact duplicate business rows only after defining the duplicate key.
Flag missing therapeutic class/unit cost and orphan encounter IDs; do not invent values.
Load cleaned output to a new table and preserve raw inputs.
challenges.starter:
Power Query M learning pattern:
Table.TransformColumns(Source, {{"drug_name", each Text.Trim(Text.Clean(_)), type text}})
Text.Upper(Text.Trim([order_status]))
Table.NestedJoin(Orders, {"encounter_id"}, Encounters, {"encounter_id"}, "Encounter", JoinKind.LeftOuter)
challenges.hint: Do not deduplicate on order_id alone if order_id is unique by design. Define business duplicate logic (e.g., encounter_id + order_date + drug_name + route + quantity) and review candidate duplicates before removal.
challenges.solution: Use the supplied `powerquery/clean_orders.m` as a reference pattern. Keep `Raw_Orders` unchanged. Add quality flags for missing class, missing cost and orphan encounter. Deduplicate only after review using a documented business key. The script is a reference and has not been executed in Power Query Desktop.
challenges.expected: Raw source controls: 151 rows; 1 missing unit cost; 1 blank therapeutic class; 1 orphan encounter reference. One duplicate-like business record is intentionally present under a different source ID.
acceptance: Raw data preserved.
Types explicit and text normalised.
Duplicate rule documented and candidates reviewed.
Missing/orphan values flagged, not silently imputed.
Refresh steps are reproducible.

challenges.title: Data validation and spreadsheet controls
challenges.scenario: A workbook is being handed to a second analyst and needs basic input controls.
tasks: Add a list validation to a controlled status field.
Highlight missing unit costs and invalid/nonpositive quantities.
Protect formula cells while leaving designated input cells editable (optional).
Add a visible data-quality summary.
challenges.starter:
Data > Data Validation > Allow: List > Source: Active,Discontinued,On Hold
Conditional formatting: =ISBLANK($I2)
Invalid quantity: =$H2<=0
challenges.hint: Use a named range or a reference list for maintainability. Validation reduces new entry errors; it does not repair existing data.
challenges.solution: Create a Status_List range and use it as the validation source. Apply conditional formatting to unit_cost_inr when blank and quantity when <=0. Add counts using COUNTBLANK, COUNTIF and COUNTIFS. Recheck pasted/imported data because validation may be bypassed by paste operations.
challenges.expected: At minimum, the supplied source has one missing cost and one missing class, and one orphan encounter reference.
acceptance: Input values constrained by a controlled list.
Quality exceptions are visible.
Validation rules are documented.
Existing imported records are separately profiled.

challenges.title: Healthcare operations KPI dashboard
challenges.scenario: Prepare a one-page monthly operations view for a nontechnical manager.
tasks: Show encounter count and mean LOS.
Show the supplied 30-day readmission flag proportion with a clear caveat.
Show order quantity and synthetic order value with units.
Add department comparison and a trend/category chart where appropriate.
Add reporting period, source, refresh date and definitions.
challenges.starter:
Encounter count = COUNTA(tblEncounters[encounter_id])
Mean LOS = AVERAGE(tblEncounters[length_of_stay_days])
Supplied flag proportion = SUM(tblEncounters[readmission_30d_flag])/COUNTA(tblEncounters[encounter_id])
Order quantity = SUM(tblRawOrders[quantity])
Synthetic value = SUM(tblRawOrders[line_total_inr])
challenges.hint: Do not call the supplied flag proportion a validated readmission rate. Do not label order quantity as dispensed or administered quantity. Distinguish missing cost from zero cost.
challenges.solution: Use KPI cards for count, mean LOS, supplied flag proportion, total ordered quantity and synthetic order value. Include a note: `Synthetic training data; readmission flag is supplied and not independently validated; order quantity is not dispensing or administration; costs are synthetic.` Add department bar chart and a PivotTable-backed status mix chart.
challenges.expected: 80 encounters; mean LOS 3.875 days; supplied flag proportion 8.75%; total order quantity 3,038; synthetic order value INR 100,279.75 (missing-cost rows excluded).
acceptance: Every KPI has unit, denominator and definition.
Caveats visible on dashboard.
Charts are readable and not misleading.
Dashboard totals match reference checks.

challenges.title: Excel–SQL reconciliation and timed interview task
challenges.scenario: A remote client requests a reproducible department operations summary before a deadline.
tasks: Within 45 minutes, profile the files and identify quality issues.
Create department-level encounter counts and mean LOS.
Create therapeutic-class order counts after documented cleaning.
Reconcile total encounter count and order quantity with SQL/Python reference checks.
Write a concise handoff with definitions, caveats and unresolved issues.
challenges.hint: Use `healthcare_sql_mastery.db` for encounter/order source counts and SQL comparisons. The Excel-specific source includes additional deliberately imperfect fields; compare like-for-like source versions and cleaning rules.
challenges.solution: A passing handoff reports 80 encounters, 151 raw order rows, mean LOS 3.875 days, supplied readmission flag 7/80 = 8.75%, raw ordered quantity 3,038 and synthetic value INR 100,279.75. It explicitly reports one missing cost, one blank class and one orphan encounter reference. The duplicate-like row requires a documented business key decision; do not silently delete it.
challenges.expected: 100-point rubric: accuracy 30; cleaning/quality controls 20; formulas/PivotTables 15; reconciliation 15; communication/caveats 10; reproducibility/file hygiene 10. Target >=75; redo any critical denominator or grain error.
acceptance: 45-minute timer respected.
Outputs reconcile to stated source grain.
Quality issues and caveats are explicit.
Handoff is concise and reproducible.
Workbook and source files are organised for client review.
